messages:
maya_support: Hey team — customer TieredAnalytics reported that their daily usage CSV (export) and the Console daily chart disagree by one day for a subset of rows. They say calls around midnight local time (America/Los_Angeles) show up under the next day in the CSV but correctly in the Console. Sample CSV attached by customer (see lines 23-28) shows timestamps like 2025-05-02T23:58:12Z attributed to 2025-05-03 in the export. They’re worried about billing reconciliation. Can someone triage?
jordan_be: Thanks, Maya. Do we know which field the CSV uses to bucket the day — event_time vs ingestion_time? Also, is the export documented to be in UTC?
maya_support: Customer expects export to respect account timezone (their org setting is America/Los_Angeles). Console chart uses account timezone and matches customer expectation. They say export looks like it was bucketed by UTC day.
lee_data: @jordan_be quick note: our export job historically runs as a daily job at 00:05 UTC and uses the exported table "usage_rollup_v2" which has both event_ts and ingest_ts. I’ll pull the job and confirm which column we use.
ingest-bot: export-job-1765123456: completed export for org_id=4382, file=/exports/org_4382/usage_2025-05-03.csv :white_check_mark:
jordan_be: Can you paste the snippet of the export SQL from the job? suspect we might be doing DATE(ingest_ts) instead of converting event_ts to org timezone.
lee_data: Pasted from CI job: ```sql
SELECT
  org_id,
  user_id,
  DATE(ingest_ts) as usage_date,
  sum(tokens) as tokens
FROM usage_events_staging
WHERE ingest_date = current_date - INTERVAL '1 day'
GROUP BY org_id, user_id, DATE(ingest_ts);
```
lee_data: That looks wrong if the org wants local days. ingest_ts is UTC ingestion time and the job runs in UTC window, so events near local midnight will fall on the next UTC day.
maya_support: Customer provided repro steps: 1) turn on CSV export for May 3 2) query for all events with event_ts between 2025-05-02T23:30:00-07:00 and 2025-05-03T00:30:00-07:00 3) compare Console chart day buckets vs CSV. They did that and found mismatch.
jordan_be: Proposed fix: change the rollup to compute usage_date as DATE(event_ts AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AT TIME ZONE org_tz) or equivalent in our SQL layer, pulling org_tz from org_profile. Example: ```DATE((event_ts AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE org_tz) AS usage_date``` That will align CSV with Console which does similar conversion for charts.
lee_data: Agree. Two follow-ups: 1) we need to backfill the last 7 days for affected orgs before they download again, 2) ensure scheduled export job uses org timezone mapping when batching files (not just the rollup). Backfill will be a separate job against the rollup table.
maya_support: Customer asked if there’s any workaround now — they want immediate reconciliation.
jordan_be: Short-term workaround: ask customer to re-run export but with our API parameter &tz=America/Los_Angeles (we actually support tz param for the ad-hoc CSV endpoint). I can enable a one-off export for them if they confirm org_id and preferred tz.
lee_data: I'll open PR to change rollup SQL and add unit tests for timezone mapping. Plan: patch -> staging canary -> backfill for orgs with activity in midnight window -> prod deploy.
maya_support: Thanks. I’ll reply to customer: offer the one-off tz-aware export via API and say engineering is fixing the rollup and will backfill 7 days. Will provide ETA. :thumbsup:
jordan_be: ETA for patch + canary: 48 hours. Backfill ETA depends on size; for org 4382 it should be couple hours. I’ll add a note to the incident tracker.
lee_data: Adding to PR: include a small migration to mark which exports were generated using ingest_date so support can flag potentially mismatched files.
maya_support: Perfect — I’ll keep customer updated and ask for sample account id confirmation. Closing loop here for now. :eyes:
